newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares chase records again, watch U.S..
newsitem.headline: German shares chase records again, watch U.S..

text.p: German shares were back in record chasing form in afternoon trade on Wednesday, buoyed by data seen indicating a lower risk of an imminent U.S. rate hike.

The IBIS DAX index was up 37.65 points, or more than one percent, at 3,596.94, having spiked as high as 3,601.64 points after data was released showing an unexpected large drop in U.S. producer prices in April.
Dealers said the market looked like testing new record territory, but said its performance depended to a large extent on how U.S. shares react to the inflation report.
Futures were driving the cash market, dealers warned, meaning that prices could also retreat rapidly if the U.S. market reaction is muted.
"Let's see what Wall Street has to offer. We need some real orders to keep this going," said one dealer.

The market mood was generally positive. Despite an apparent drop in the DAX index, which fell as it caught up with a late decline in prices during post-bourse electronic trade later, most prices were higher throughout the day.
"Telekom has been the only factor holding us back today and even that doesn't look like lasting," another dealer noted.
Deutsche Telekom sank in early trade, hitting a low of 38.01 marks as news began to emerge that the government might be keen to sell part of its stake in the telecommunications giant.
However the share recovered as it became apparent that the government was unlikely to sell a stake on the open market and Telekom was trading at 39.40 marks, down just 40 pfennigs, at 1323 GMT.
"That was really a chance to buy," said one dealer of the lows hit by the stock, which has been popular lately amid optimism for its earnings outlook in the coming years.
Deutsche Bank AG was also trading heavily as the banking sector in general came back into favour.

Some dealers said news that Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG plans to start merger talks with Norddeutsche Landesbank had attracted more interest to the sector, where talk of mergers is generally welcomed strongly.
Building group Hochtief AG led the advance in percentage terms with gains of six marks or nearly nine percent after it was raised to market outperformer from "performer" by Goldman Sachs.
